prismpath.stdout:
usage: prismpath [-h] [--version] <command> ...

Command-line interface for prismpath

positional arguments:
  <command>

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --version   show program's version number and exit

commands, by who runs them

Process owner: author and test the policy of record:
  init         Scaffold a starter flow - zero to a running, validated flow in two commands
  validate     Static analysis
  test         Assert a flow's routing from a Markdown fixture (no LLM)
  graph        Render the flow as a Mermaid diagram (solid=deterministic, dashed=semantic)
  lint         Static analysis + semantic-ambiguity check (needs the embedder)
  context      Emit the verified facts PrismPath can PROVE about a flow (nodes, edges, declared...
  policy       Write a core policy as readable rules

Engineer: implement the interface once, calibrate for deployment, deliver:
  contract     Derive each node's worker output schema from its `when` edges
  capability   Report which targets a flow compiles to (python / portable js-rust-go / Level M...
  compile      Compile a flow and its lock into a single-file portable JS bundle
  portable     Is this flow (and its @spawn children) in the ML-free portable subset? Portable...
  lock         Write a routing lockfile (committed condition embeddings) for reproducible routing
  verify       Bounded model checking over the decidable tiers
  plugins      Audit the plugin ecosystem
  ci-report    Markdown PR report for changed flows
  lsp          Language Server over stdio
  import       Import a LangGraph StateGraph (.py) as a skeleton flow (with TODO conditions)
  calibrate    Calibrate the escalation threshold tau from labeled routing decisions
  label        Hand-label routing decisions in a JSONL log (calibration data)
  annotate     Blind-label a benchmark (labels hidden) for inter-annotator kappa (gate zero)
  kappa        Cohen's kappa between two annotation files (+ adjudicated gold / disagreements)
  centroids    Cross-validate prototype/centroid routing vs zero-shot embedding on a benchmark
  authorize    Sign a Markdown flow with the policy authority key, or verify that signature
  canonicalize Write a canon/2 document a person wrote (any spacing, member order or escapes) as...

Operator: run the system day to day, swap and attest policy (Mission Control is the console; this is the scripted path):
  run          Parse the flow and run it (mock worker by default; --worker ollama:MODEL for a real...
  resume       Resume a suspended/crashed run from a JSON checkpoint (mock agent); like run, it...
  compose      Advance pending fan-out/composition runs in the queue
  swap         Secure policy hot-swap
  trail        Summarise an audit log over a window
  agent        Govern a Claude Code session
  gateway      Protect a resource
  dist         Policy distribution

Assessor: anchor, verify, and read the evidence:
  ledger       Evidence
  evidence     Verify a signed core run
  facet        Facet telemetry

`swap` splits by action: keygen, envelope, and pack are the engineer's setup; swap and attest are the operator's; verify is the assessor's. `ledger keygen` is the engineer's setup too: it makes the deployment's instance key, which signs root statements and is never the policy authority key. `authorize` splits the same way as `swap`: sign is the engineer's (it holds the authority key), verify is the assessor's.

prismpath agent.stdout:
usage: prismpath agent [-h] <action> ...

positional arguments:
  <action>
    init      make the authority and instance keys in the user config
              directory, record the signed agent_default policy, and write the
              hook entries into the project's .claude/settings.json (shown
              first; written with --yes or a y at the prompt)
    hook      what Claude Code runs: the hook JSON on stdin, the answer on
              stdout; any failure is a deny with cause agent:hook-error, never
              an allow
    verify    seal the open runs and verify every run with both keys pinned,
              every receipt replayed through the reference kernel
    status    the keys and their ids, the policy hash, the project's hook
              entries and every run with its receipt count, open or sealed
    rules     the installed policy's rules in order, each with its hits and
              last hit counted from the receipts that verify, the core's own
              refusals, the rules never matched and the rules no reading can
              reach; it changes nothing
    approvals
              the escalate rules whose asks were approved (and the call ran)
              at least N times, with counts and example readings as classes
              only: candidates for the owner to sign into the policy; it
              changes nothing and adopts nothing
    doctor    check the whole setup (key modes and pairs, the policy, the hook
              entries and their interpreter, a timed dry run, the runs, free
              disk) and print ok, warn or fail with the fixing command for
              each; it changes nothing
    zones     the owner's protected code: `set` records and signs a zone file
              (the protected names, bound to the recorded policy and the
              project), `status` says what the hook will do about zones,
              `warm` asks Context Cloud about every file so the hook answers
              from the cache
    run       run a program as the agent under the sandbox (Linux, bubblewrap
              and socat): the workspace is the only writable path, its control
              paths and the staged settings are read only, and the only way
              out is a proxy that allows the model API. A "yes, and don't ask
              again" that Claude Code would save to
              .claude/settings.local.json fails here, by design

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

prismpath agent init.stdout:
usage: prismpath agent init [-h] [--project PROJECT] [--yes] [--follow STREAM]
                            [--anchor FILE] [--confirm FINGERPRINT]
                            [--policy STARTER|FILE] [--json]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --project PROJECT     the project directory (default $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR,
                        else the current directory)
  --yes                 write the settings change without asking
  --follow STREAM       follow a policy stream instead: the home holds no
                        authority key, takes the trust anchor given with
                        --anchor, shows its fingerprint, and after --confirm
                        commits the releases the controller offers (`prismpath
                        dist`)
  --anchor FILE         with --follow: the stream's trust anchor
  --confirm FINGERPRINT
                        with --follow: the anchor's fingerprint, as the owner
                        gave it
  --policy STARTER|FILE
                        the policy to record. A starter is strict (refuses
                        what it cannot read and shell commands that change
                        files), default (asks about those), review (also asks
                        about every change inside the project) or session
                        (default, and also asks about later calls when the
                        session already changed protected code or ran many
                        shell commands). A FILE is your own rules source
                        (.rules.md) or image (.core.json), compiled and
                        checked as `prismpath policy compile --target agent`
                        checks it (default: the one recorded, else default)
  --json                machine readable output

prismpath agent run.stdout:
usage: prismpath agent run [-h] [--workspace WORKSPACE] [--credential FILE]
                           [--egress-log FILE] [--max-processes MAX_PROCESSES]
                           [--allow-host HOST]
                           [--local-model http://HOST:PORT] [--ro PATH]
                           ...

positional arguments:
  program               -- PROGRAM [ARGS]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --workspace WORKSPACE
                        the directory the agent may write (default: the
                        current directory)
  --credential FILE     copy this one file into the sandbox as its Claude
                        credential (off unless given; PrismPath never looks
                        for a login of its own)
  --egress-log FILE     keep the proxy's log of every connection attempt here
                        (default: in the run directory of the egress run,
                        beside its receipts)
  --max-processes MAX_PROCESSES
                        the process limit inside the sandbox
  --allow-host HOST     a host name the policy may allow on port 443 (net_dest
                        allowed_host); repeatable. The digest of the sorted
                        list is recorded with the run
  --local-model http://HOST:PORT
                        a fixed route to one local model server: the sandbox
                        reaches only that host and port, at 127.0.0.1:PORT
                        inside, and each use is logged (a separate route, not
                        a proxy exception)
  --ro PATH             also show this host path to the program, read only
                        (repeatable)

prismpath dist.stdout:
usage: prismpath dist [-h] <action> ...

positional arguments:
  <action>
    seal         sign the envelopes of a release from a signed policy manifest
                 with --manifest, or one envelope for a body from flags (the
                 owner, where the key is)
    widen        sign the widening statement a release that allows more needs
                 (W4)
    anchor       write the trust anchor of a stream from authority public keys
    install      seal an install set: an action floor, a fallback policy or a
                 ceiling (section 21)
    install-trust
                 seal an install trust statement (IS11)
    verify       run the verifier on a sealed envelope and its body
    serve        run the reference controller's HTTP listener on its directory
    enroll       enrol a PEP by its instance public key, and serve its stream
    acknowledge  acknowledge a held install set or install trust statement by
                 the envelope ids of its statements, so the controller offers
                 it (H13)
    offer        offer a stored release to a group
    commit       send commit to the members of a group's rollout that staged
    abort        end a group's rollout and send abort to its members
    fleet        print the fleet view (F4), or export its state records and
                 findings
    revoke       seal the next revocation list (the owner, where the key is)
    rotate       seal a key rotation, signed by a trusted key and the new one
    rekey        rotate, release under the new key, commit, then revoke the
                 old key
    pep          run a host enforcement point (provision, poll, status,
                 rollback)

options:
  -h, --help     show this help message and exit

                        an envelope id of the set, repeatable; name every

prismpath dist anchor.stdout:
usage: prismpath dist anchor [-h] --pub FILE --target TARGET --stream STREAM
                             [--controller FILE] [--fresh SECONDS]
                             [--install-pub FILE]
                             [--install-threshold INSTALL_THRESHOLD]
                             [--operator-pub FILE] [--install-seq INSTALL_SEQ]
                             [--domain SHA256] --out FILE

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --pub FILE            an authority public key, 32 raw bytes (`swap keygen`),
                        repeatable
  --target TARGET       the target kind of the stream's PEPs
  --stream STREAM
  --controller FILE     the controller's instance public key, 32 raw bytes;
                        writes a prismpath.dist-trust/2 anchor that names it
                        as the first controller key (K6, P4)
  --fresh SECONDS       with --controller, the longest lifetime of a fresh
                        statement; 0 leaves freshness off (H16)
  --install-pub FILE    an install public key, 32 raw bytes, repeatable;
                        writes the anchor's install part (P4)
  --install-threshold INSTALL_THRESHOLD
                        the install threshold (IS2)
  --operator-pub FILE   an operator public key, 32 raw bytes, repeatable (OP1)
  --install-seq INSTALL_SEQ
                        the install trust sequence the keys stand at
  --domain SHA256       the hash of the reading domain the PEP was built with
                        (P4, CL4); default the one this build gives the target
                        kind
  --out FILE

prismpath dist install.stdout:
usage: prismpath dist install [-h] --kind {floor,fallback,ceiling}
                              [--set AS=FILE] [--list FILE] [--empty] --stream
                              STREAM --seq SEQ --target TARGET --key PEM
                              [--not-before NOT_BEFORE] [--qualification FILE]
                              [--follows DIR] [--ceiling DIR] [--widens]
                              [--yes] [--held DIR] [--staged] [--canary GROUP]
                              [--rate ALLOWS/WINDOW]
                              [--answer-rate ALLOWS/WINDOW] [--layout FILE]
                              [--command COMMAND_REGISTER] --out DIR

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --kind {floor,fallback,ceiling}
                        the install kind: an action floor, a fallback policy
                        or a ceiling
  --set AS=FILE         an artifact of the set and its body, repeatable, such
                        as policy.ppt=table.ppt
  --list FILE           for a ceiling of a kind that cannot decide, a table
                        the list holds, repeatable (CL1)
  --empty               the empty set, which withdraws the held one (IS6)
  --stream STREAM
  --seq SEQ             the install sequence of this kind on the stream
  --target TARGET       the one target kind of the set (IS1)
  --key PEM             an install private key
  --not-before NOT_BEFORE
                        Unix seconds (default now)
  --qualification FILE  for a policy.ppt, fill its meta from the image and
                        this qualification envelope
  --follows DIR         the set this one follows, as this command wrote it;
                        sets replaces and is compared (IS12)
  --ceiling DIR         the held ceiling, as this command wrote it (CL3)
  --widens              say the set allows more than the one it follows
  --yes                 sign the install change statement for a floor or
                        fallback table the comparator finds allows nothing
                        more, and a ceiling after its lapse preview, without
                        asking at the terminal (IS15, CL5)
  --held DIR            a controller directory, read and never written: a
                        ceiling's lapse preview names the releases it is above
                        and the machines that run each (CL5, CL6)
  --staged              a ceiling for a planned change: the controller offers
                        it to the canary group first and to the rest once the
                        canary reports it applied with no unexpected lapse
                        (CL7)
  --canary GROUP        with --staged, the controller group offered the
                        ceiling first (default canary)
  --rate ALLOWS/WINDOW  a floor's signed rate of overrides (AF8)
  --answer-rate ALLOWS/WINDOW
                        a floor's signed rate of operator allows (OP4)
  --layout FILE         a table floor's layout document (AF10)
  --command COMMAND_REGISTER
                        a table floor's command register (AF9)
  --out DIR             where each <as>.sealed and <as>.body is written

prismpath dist install-trust.stdout:
usage: prismpath dist install-trust [-h] --current-pub FILE
                                    --current-threshold CURRENT_THRESHOLD
                                    [--current-operator FILE] --install-pub
                                    FILE [--operator-pub FILE] --threshold
                                    THRESHOLD --retired FILE --stream STREAM
                                    --seq SEQ --target TARGET --key PEM
                                    [--not-before NOT_BEFORE] --out FILE

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --current-pub FILE    an install public key as the PEP holds it now,
                        repeatable
  --current-threshold CURRENT_THRESHOLD
  --current-operator FILE
  --install-pub FILE    a key of the new set
  --operator-pub FILE
  --threshold THRESHOLD
  --retired FILE        the engineer's list of every retired key id, one per

                        retired is never added again
  --stream STREAM
  --seq SEQ             the install trust sequence, the held one plus one
  --target TARGET
  --key PEM             a signer: the current install keys at the threshold
                        and every key the statement adds
  --not-before NOT_BEFORE
                        Unix seconds (default now)
  --out FILE            the sealed statement; the body goes beside it

  --dir DIR             the controller's directory

prismpath dist revoke.stdout:

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --entry KIND=VALUE    add envelope=<id>, policy=<hash> or key=<key id>
                        (repeatable)
  --drop KIND=VALUE     leave out an envelope or a policy a floor has passed
                        (repeatable)
  --floor STREAM=SEQ    raise a floor (repeatable)
  --seq SEQ             the trust sequence (default the held one plus one)

                             [--target TARGET] --key PEM --held DIR
                             [--not-before NOT_BEFORE] --out FILE

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --new PEM             the new authority private key
  --retire KEY_ID       a trusted key id to retire
  --seq SEQ             the trust sequence (default the held one plus one)
  --target TARGET       a target kind (default every served kind)

prismpath dist seal.stdout:
usage: prismpath dist seal [-h] [--manifest FILE] [--pub PUB] [--revoked JSON]
                           [--state-dir DIR] [--artifact ARTIFACT]
                           [--body FILE] [--stream STREAM] [--seq SEQ]
                           [--target TARGET] [--not-before NOT_BEFORE]
                           [--expires EXPIRES] --key PEM [--held DIR] --out
                           FILE [--release RELEASE] [--policy SHA256]
                           [--replaces SHA256] [--widens] [--yes]
                           [--meta FILE] [--qualification FILE]
                           [--ceiling DIR]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --manifest FILE       a signed policy manifest (<name>.policy.md): check it
                        as `policy manifest check` does and seal one envelope
                        per artifact of each target's release into the --out
                        directory; the stream, seq, targets, times, widens and
                        replaces come from it, not from flags; --out is a new
                        or empty directory
  --pub PUB             with --manifest, a trusted authority public key that
                        may have signed it (repeatable)
  --revoked JSON        with --manifest, the revocation list of authority key
                        ids
  --state-dir DIR       with --manifest, and required with it: the version
                        floor, so a manifest signed below the version sealed
                        before is refused, and the floor is raised once the
                        envelopes are written
  --artifact ARTIFACT   the artifact kind, such as policy.ppt (the flag form)
  --body FILE           the body (the flag form)
  --stream STREAM
  --seq SEQ
  --target TARGET       a target kind (repeatable)
  --not-before NOT_BEFORE
                        Unix seconds (default now)
  --expires EXPIRES     Unix seconds; 0 (the default) only for a trust kind
  --key PEM             an authority private key (repeatable)
  --held DIR            a controller directory, for R8
  --out FILE            where the sealed envelope is written (with seal
                        --manifest, a directory)
  --release RELEASE     the release id (default the release of this one
                        artifact)
  --policy SHA256       the policy hash (default the body's own)
  --replaces SHA256     the policy hash this release replaces (default, with
                        --held, the latest release stored on the stream below
                        this seq, else none)
  --widens              say the release allows more than the one it replaces;
                        set as well unless the release is compared with the
                        one --held holds for replaces and is not larger (W7)
  --yes                 sign the change statement for a table the comparator
                        finds allows nothing more, without asking (W9, W11)
  --meta FILE           the meta object, JSON
  --qualification FILE  for policy.ppt, fill meta from the image and this
                        qualification envelope
  --ceiling DIR         the ceiling the stream's PEPs hold, as `dist install`
                        wrote it; a release above it is refused before it is
                        sealed (CL2)

  --json                machine readable output
  --pub INSTANCE_PUB [INSTANCE_PUB ...]
                        pin the deployment's instance public key(s): every
                        root statement must be signed by one, and a log with
                        no statements is invalid rather than unsigned
  --statements PATH     the root statements file (default: beside the log,
                        run.audit.jsonl -> run.audit.roots.jsonl)
  --receipt IDX         check one receipt offline: leaf -> inclusion path ->
                        signed root -> signature -> key; --json prints the
                        self contained bundle
  --bundle-out FILE     with --receipt: write that receipt's bundle to FILE,
                        for a reader to check with --verify-bundle
  --verify-bundle FILE  check a receipt bundle from FILE (a --bundle-out file,
                        or the --json report of --receipt) without the log:
                        receipt -> leaf -> inclusion path -> signed root ->
                        signature -> key, result signed | signed-unpinned |
                        invalid (exit 0, 0, 1). Offline, except the anchor
                        step: --anchor-dir runs `ots verify`, which needs
                        Bitcoin block data (a node or an explorer)
  --anchor-dir DIR      with --verify-bundle: also check the statement's hash
                        is in the batch `ledger anchor --statements --out DIR`
                        stamped, and that its OpenTimestamps proof verifies
  --label LABEL         the anchor label (default v1), with --anchor-dir

usage: prismpath validate [-h] [--json] flow_md

positional arguments:
  flow_md     Path to the flow markdown file

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      machine-readable findings

prismpath verify.stdout:
usage: prismpath verify [-h] [--reach NODE] [--forbid NODE] [--assume EXPR]
                        [--bound BOUND] [--no-errors] [--no-events]
                        [--level-m] [--json]
                        flow_md

positional arguments:
  flow_md        Path to the flow markdown file

options:
  -h, --help     show this help message and exit
  --reach NODE   assert NODE is reachable (exit 1 if not); repeatable
  --forbid NODE  assert NODE can NEVER be reached (exit 1 if reachable or may-
                 reachable); repeatable
  --assume EXPR  a `when`-style constraint every worker outcome satisfies,
                 e.g. --assume "amount <= 500"
  --bound BOUND  search depth limit in steps (default 25, the engine max_steps
                 default)
  --no-errors    exclude error-tier paths (assume workers never raise)
  --no-events    exclude event-tier paths (assume suspended runs are never
                 resumed)
  --level-m      also report per-edge match-action fragment membership (SPEC
                 §4.3)
  --json         machine-readable output
